questions.title: Run-Length Encode a String
questions.description:
Read a single line containing only lowercase letters and print its **run-length encoding**.

### Input
One line: a string of lowercase letters (`a`-`z`).
```
aaabbc
```

### Output
One line, with no spaces or separators: each maximal run of the same repeated character, written as the character followed immediately by how many times it repeats in a row.
```
a3b2c1
```

**Important:** this includes runs of length 1 — a character that does not repeat still gets a `1` after it (for example, the `c` in `aaabbc` appears once, so it becomes `c1`, not just `c`).

### Worked example
Input `aaabbc` breaks into three runs: `aaa` (a, repeated 3 times), `bb` (b, repeated 2 times), `c` (c, repeated 1 time). Concatenating each run's character with its count gives `a3b2c1`.

starterCode.python:
import sys

line = sys.stdin.readline().rstrip('\n')

# TODO: walk through `line`, tracking the current character and how many
# times it repeats in a row (its "run"). Each time the next character is
# different from the current run's character, append the run's character
# plus its count (as a string) to the result, then start a new run with
# the new character. Don't forget to flush the final run once the loop
# finishes.
#
# Print the encoded string with print() -- one line, no separators
# between runs, and runs of length 1 still end with "1".

testCases.description: normal case with mixed run lengths
single repeated character, one long run
run of length 11, proving multi-digit counts work
longer mixed input with several runs
